questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was looking for a good university with lots of opportunities for outdoor activities

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Was fairly straightforward to be honest

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an exchange student intro day which introduced you to different clubs and activities at the university. Good opportunity to make some acquaintances. There was also a bunch of speeches and information that was a waste of time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was kind of difficult to find housing. I basically didn't even try to look for housing via the university since I was told that's mainly for freshmen. So I just joined a few facebook housing groups for the city and kept posting there. Got lots of positive replies, however, the issues was that I was only going for 1 semester and almost every single room is on a year long lease. I happened to eventually find a person who was also going on exchange for a semester so I got his room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start searching early so that you have options. Find yourself some roommates that you're compatible with. Also, Boulder is damn expensive. Maybe don't worry too much about getting a nice kitchen since you can eat well at the cantines on campus (c4c).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I signed up for all my courses online before arriving. I had to send proof for prerequisites to Boulder, which was a bit clumsy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a dialogue with the economics counsellor at Boulder who was very helpful. She contacted me via my KU-mail at some point.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just do it in advance. There's not as many courses as at KU, so if you leave it till late, you might end up stuck with a course you're not interested in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is much much lower than at KU. If you're planning on going there for academics, don't. Perhaps the graduate level courses are more challenging, I'm not sure. However, I'm pretty sure they are very time consuming and difficult to get into. The good thing is that if you're going to Boulder for a great experience, then you'll have plenty of time to enjoy yourself there, since you won't need to spend much time on your studies.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We didn't have lectures and exercise classes like at KU. We essentially just had one type of class where the professor was giving a lecture but it was in classrooms with perhaps 30 people, so there was ample opportunity to ask questions. As a matter of fact they expect you to do so much more than at KU. I honestly kind of liked this aspect as you perhaps have fewer people just sleeping through class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Natural Resource Economics
Industrial Organization and Regulation
Antitrust and Regulation
Economics of Entrepreneurship

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Natural Resource Economics is taught by an enthusiastic professor, Daniel Kaffine. Antitrust and Regulation will be of interest to you if you're less into math and more into law, as all the case studies are based on court cases where economists and lawyers work together. Economics of Entrepreneurship is massive a waste of time.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is super pricy there but you can eat at c4c on campus. Phone service was also really expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The gym is mindblowing. It's called the Rec Center and it's 3 stories and has tennis courts, basketball courts, running track, ice rink, swimming pool, martial arts gyms, and an endless supply of weightlifting and fitness equipment.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: You can go climbing, hiking, mountain biking, river rafting, camping, skiing. Join the clubs at uni and you'll have plenty of people to go with.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went on a road trip to Arizona and Utah to see the deserts and national parks there. Also, I went to Washington State to see the Hoh Rainforest and to Wyoming for Yellowstone. Closer to Boulder you can go to Rocky Mountains National Park, which has beautiful hikes to Bear Lake and Chasm Lake. I think on the latter there's people who climb up to it once it freezes over and play ice hockey on it. I didn't get to see the Sand Dunes but that's supposed to be really cool as well. You should go to Meow Wolf in Denver that place is sick. Also, if you're into it go check out the Clocktower Cabaret in Denver.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not very hard.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Partake and engage in their local activities I guess.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You can't drink in public. Also, people are perhaps slightly less mature than in Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people there are really kind and welcoming. You can walk up to any person and make friends basically. They're much more open to talking to strangers.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make friends with lots of other exchange students early on as people settle into their own groups later. You can do this by joining various clubs.
Figure out the housing and courses well in advance.
And just enjoy your stay there without worrying too much about school.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making new friends and camping and getting to explore new places.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: You'll need to get around by car to visit some of the places outside the city. I was just interchangeably borrowing my roomies cars. So if you don't have a driver's license getting around might be a challenge. Also, everything is damn pricy so save up some money before going because you don't want to be saying no to cool experiences while you're there that you might not get to do again.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
